### 2.1 Census-vs-outdir layering (why the census cites calibration witnesses)

The census contains zero references to the generation-4 outdir. This is the
designed layering, not an omission: the gen-4 outdir banks the *campaign*
artifacts (benchmark rows, timings, judgment, seeds), while the parity
census re-derives from the sealed floor-table **calibration witnesses**.
Witness-dir distribution over the 168 lines (grep+uniq):

| witness dir | refs | serves |
|---|---|---|
| `m7_floor_calibration_p7cap_20261025-125823` | 126 | the six gen-2 post-cap faces |
| `m7_floor_calibration_p7cap_20261104T093543Z` | 21 | `sigminer_post_v3_rust_batch` (gen-3) |
| `m7_floor_calibration_p7cap_legacy_20261027-083955` | 21 | `sigminer` (pre-law gen-2 face) |
| `m7_floor_calibration_p7cap_legacy_20261111-144552` | 168 | the yardstick (sigprofiler SS3 re-mint) |

The `attestation=pre-law` stamp on every line is the SS3-era posture:
witnesses re-stamped in place onto epoch `cfdcc51dbb9b7041` (only
`attestation.epoch` differs), with the pre-law measurement inadmissibility
documented in the memo §3 — the witnesses are admissible as floor anchors,
their timing law predates the cap regime and the census says so on every
line.
